rationale: Reviewed the full BRIEF, spec.md and ADR-0045 at 7a490064, with G2's trust-boundary lens. The design preserves important git corroboration guards, and ordinary forgeability of repo files is explicitly within ADR-0037's accepted anti-footgun boundary. However, the spec gives selection, readiness and dependency scoping incompatible spec-identity authorities, and promotes pre-existing override metadata into claim authority without defining how the new evidence requirement applies. These are spec-contract gaps that can produce either unclaimable advertised members or fail-open readiness decisions. Scratch-only probes against the unchanged resolver reproduced the identity mismatch; eight focused real-git landed-evidence regression tests and three existing readiness/marker tests passed. These tests ground the review in the current tree; they do not test the proposed implementation, which this commit does not contain. No source-repository mutations were made.
concrete_changes_required: Amend R1/R3 and the readiness integration contract so a metadata.spec_id-only member with a neutral title can actually be claimed without an override. Define one effective spec context shared by selection, EvaluateReadiness and dispatch, and define what happens when metadata, epic lineage and an explicit --spec disagree. Never validate one spec's plan/dependencies and then dispatch the bead into another spec. Add claim-path ACs for a parentless metadata-only bead with no spec title, and for metadata pointing to S while parent/title resolve to T; either use the same explicitly defined context throughout or refuse the conflict before mutation.

Rewrite R4.1 to use a status-independent descendant-or-metadata membership check for CLOSED dependencies, rather than the ready-only SpecMembers result or an unchanged FindEpicForBead fallback. Distinguish positively established non-membership from lookup/JSON/metadata errors; errors must not become the 'not applicable' PASS. Extend AC-9 with a closed metadata-only same-spec dependency lacking a merge (FAIL), a closed descendant with no title linkage (FAIL without a merge), and membership-read failures (refuse/indeterminate, never PASS). State explicitly how genuine plain-task/no-lineage results are distinguished from failures.

Define R6.3's marker-admission and legacy-marker policy before granting stored metadata claim authority. The current writer emits only signals and overridden, with no evidence. Prefer requiring a valid evidence-bearing marker for automatic reuse, with an explicit recovery to re-record legacy or incomplete markers using the scoped flag and evidence file. Specify validation of signal IDs, timestamp and evidence snapshot consistency (sha256/bytes/text), and fail closed on malformed records or read failures. Add ACs for legacy evidence-free markers, incomplete or inconsistent evidence, malformed signals and metadata-read errors, alongside the valid-marker subset cases. No signature or tamper-proof storage is requested; this is about enforcing the new evidence contract at every bypass ingress.

findings.title: New selection membership does not reach the readiness trust boundary
findings.detail: spec.md R1.1 (line 92) makes a metadata.spec_id-only bead selectable whatever its title says, and AC-1 requires claiming that bead. But GateReadiness calls readiness.EvaluateReadiness, which calls phase.FindEpicForBead and refuses if it cannot resolve lineage. FindEpicForBeadWithCache reads epic dependencies, then falls back to a title-number match; it does not read the bead's metadata.spec_id. The spec does not require this owning-context path to change, and lists internal/phase derivation as out of scope. A review-only seam probe in scratch repo/internal/phase/g2_trust_probe_test.go, run with go test ./internal/phase -run TestG2SpecLinkageAuthorityProbe -v, passed three observations: metadata.spec_id=129-readiness-tracker-honesty plus a neutral title/no parent returns ErrNoEpicLineage; the same metadata plus title '[777] Foreign title' resolves 777-foreign; the same metadata plus a foreign epic also resolves 777-foreign. Thus the new membership promise either fails at the gate or the gate checks foreign artifacts. cmd/mindspec/next.go later passes the explicit specFlag to EnsureWorktree/DispatchBead, so a mismatched gate context is not merely display drift. A writable linkage key needs a defined context/conflict contract, not just SpecID syntax validation.

findings.title: Closed-dependency applicability is specified using incompatible membership mechanisms
findings.detail: R4.1 (line 113) says a closed dependency is checked only if it is a member per R1.1, resolved through existing findEpicForBeadFn lineage, never by title. R1.1's concrete predicate queries bd ready on both union legs, so a closed dependency is absent from that result regardless of its membership. The existing lineage resolver is not an equivalent substitute: it ignores metadata.spec_id and contains a title fallback. If absence from the ready projection or failure to discover lineage is interpreted as non-membership, a closed, unmerged dependency linked only by metadata will now PASS on bd-closed alone. That changes today's fail-closed MF-3 into a false PASS for a dependency the new selection contract explicitly treats as belonging to the spec. AC-9 covers same-spec/foreign/plain-task examples but does not pin metadata-only closed membership or read-error handling. The spec must separate membership from readiness and distinguish unknown from proven foreign membership.

findings.title: Existing-marker reuse bypasses the newly required evidence contract
findings.detail: R6.2 (line 127) requires an evidence file for a scoped override, but R6.3 (line 128) authorizes ready-check success and later re-claims solely when failing signal IDs are recorded. RecordReadinessOverride currently writes {signals, overridden}; TestRecordReadinessOverride_WritesMarkerViaMergeMetadata passed against that current schema. Every legitimate legacy marker therefore lacks the new evidence snapshot, yet the proposed read rule admits it and GateReadiness would claim without --evidence or a fresh scoped flag. No schema/legacy/error admission rule or negative AC closes this alternate bypass ingress. This is a new binary authorization use: current GateReadiness evaluates and refuses without the explicit boolean override, and does not consult stored markers. The concern is not that a bd user could deliberately forge a fully valid record; it is that ordinary old or incomplete records silently evade the contract introduced here.

findings.title: Forgeability is accepted, but corroboration and audit are distinct from authentication
findings.detail: metadata.spec_id, override metadata and panel.json are writable by agents/bd users; an evidence file is supplied by the bypassing caller, and its SHA-256 proves snapshot consistency rather than the truth of its justification or the writer's authority. A registration is not an approved verdict: panel.Scan/ForBead read parseable matching registrations without tallying approval, and R4.3 explicitly considers every matching SHA, including registrations whose abandoned status is not filtered. These properties already fit the repo's ADR-0037 section 8 anti-footgun boundary; signing files or treating registration SHA equality as proof of panel approval would misstate that boundary. Merge subjects are likewise forgeable by a git-history writer, which ADR-0041 places outside the defended history threat model. Within that model, R4.2/R4.3 still require a reachable two-parent subject-owned candidate, exact second-parent corroboration, branch/binding contradictions to remain vetoes, and revert/ambiguity guards. I ran eight focused existing landed-merge tests covering spoofed subjects, ancestor-only panels, nonexistent/foreign/anonymous bindings, inconsistent binding pairs and masked reverts; all passed. Those guards must retain the semantics the requirements say are unchanged. No additional anti-forgery mechanism is requested.

findings.title: Errors in this BRIEF
findings.detail: The generated 'Your job' header instructs reviewers to write <slot>-round-1.json beside BRIEF, conflicting with the explicit prompt's required scratch/verdict.json destination and read-only repository restriction. I followed the prompt. The initial Summary, Files in Scope, Acceptance Criteria, Prior-Round Asks and Lens sections remain TODO placeholders and are then duplicated by filled sections. The filled scope and G2 row are usable, and the stated reviewed commit matches repository HEAD.
